title: C. Split DNS, two WAF listeners, one governed origin
subtitle: Corporate and internet clients use the same approved hostname, certificate and APIM policy. Private and public test paths were exercised; corporate hub transit and production high availability remain reference designs.

groups.title: Two client network boundaries - same hostname, signed identity and trust requirements
Regional WAF and private origins - neither ingress path bypasses APIM or its budgets
Split DNS and private service dependencies - verify both paths after every change
Optional enterprise controls - priced and reviewed separately; no implicit governance exceptions

nodes.title: Internet developer
lines: Public DNS -> selected WAF public IP.
HTTPS/443, developer Entra bearer token; trusted certificate.
One client endpoint; no direct Foundry credential. Corporate egress restrictions require their own reviewed rule.

nodes.title: Microsoft Entra ID
lines: Both client networks need public HTTPS/443 sign-in and token refresh.
Delegated OAuth; existing MFA/Conditional Access policy.
Corporate source IP is not a substitute for a signed person identity.

nodes.title: Corporate or routed spoke client
lines: Private DNS -> WAF private frontend.
HTTPS/443, same hostname, certificate and developer token.
VPN/ExpressRoute and peering are reference dependencies. The private test used a separate Azure verifier.

nodes.title: One WAF, dual HTTPS listeners
lines: [[edge]]
[[waf]]
Public and private frontends, dedicated edge subnet.
Both routes apply the same global/Messages WAF controls and trusted client-IP rewrite.
TLS re-encryption, SSE buffering off; no direct APIM shortcut for private clients.

nodes.title: One Standard v2 origin
lines: Microsoft.ApiManagement/service
Inbound private endpoint; public access disabled.
HTTPS/443 from the selected edge; unchanged person bearer. Source filter, JWT, entitlement and budgets.
Separate outbound integration in Microsoft.Web/serverFarms subnet.
HTTPS/443 to Foundry under APIM managed identity.

nodes.title: One private Foundry account
lines: Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts
Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints, account subresource.
Public network access disabled; APIM MI has scoped inference access.
Response returns on the caller's chosen WAF path.
A direct Foundry exception bypasses entitlement, budgets and the gateway ledger; none is enabled here.

nodes.title: Separate, discovered subnets
lines: Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks
[[nsg]]
Dedicated edge; exclusive APIM integration; separate private endpoints.
Separate delegated verifier subnet for evaluation, removed afterwards.
Review existing route tables, peerings and IPAM. A VNet's name does not prove hub transit.

nodes.title: Same TLS identity on both paths
lines: Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults
[[certificate-identity]]
Edge MI: HTTPS/443 via vault PE; scoped role and versionless certificate reference.
Private operators need a routed workstation. Subscription Owner is not a network tunnel.

nodes.title: Split-name resolution
lines: [[dns-a]]
Exact listener-name private zone and VNet link; public DNS retains the public WAF address.
Service private zones resolve APIM, Foundry and vault. DNS UDP/TCP 53.
Do not shadow an entire shared public namespace. Resolver endpoints have their own exclusive subnets.

nodes.title: Compare both paths
lines: Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces and Microsoft.Insights/components
Azure-managed diagnostics and authorized HTTPS/443 queries.
Check actual TLS, completed SSE and authenticated origin bypass denial from both networks.
Historical identity is not a reachability guarantee. Masked or missing IPs require explicit unknown-impact acknowledgement.

nodes.title: Optional estate, explicit choices
lines: Resolver Function -> Cosmos DB: HTTPS/443 with reader MI.
Turnstile App Service -> PostgreSQL: TLS/5432, separate integration and private data path.
Container Apps jobs -> ARM/logs: HTTPS/443 with scoped workload MI.
Each has its own network review. No tenant-admin Graph grant is implied by the gateway profile.

nodes.title: Not automatic failover or HA
lines: A second APIM instance needs policy, entitlement and DNS synchronization; quota counters are per instance.
Firewall, DNS resolver, Bastion, AKS and injected agents remain reference-only additions.
Front Door has public ingress, not this dual private/public listener design.
Premium v2 zone redundancy is a creation-time platform choice, not a selectable unit-to-zone drawing.

notice: Live: public client and private Azure verifier resolved the intended frontends and completed TLS/SSE; private direct APIM returned 403. The later private-only cutover refused internet TLS. No production HA, corporate VPN, failover or optional-estate migration is claimed.
